questions.question: Which amongst the following statements is correct about Mughal emperor Akbar?
questions.option_1: He fought and won the third battle of Panipat against the Hindu King Hemu.
questions.option_2: He founded a new religion called ‘Din-e Ilahi'.
questions.option_4: He was highly educated and knew many languages.
questions.solution:
• Akbar's Religion: He founded a new religion called ‘Din-e Ilahi'.
  • Fact: Akbar was an illiterate but highly intellectual ruler. He won the 2nd Battle of Panipat (1556), not the 3rd.

questions.question: Mahavir Jayanti celebrates the birthday of Lord Mahavira who is the _______ Tirthankara of Jainism.
questions.solution:
• Lord Mahavira: 24th
  • Detail: He was the last Tirthankara of Jainism, born in Kundagrama near Vaishali.

questions.question: Brahmo Samaj was earlier known as:
questions.solution:
• Brahmo Samaj Origin: Bramho Sabha
  • History: Founded as Brahmo Sabha in 1828, it was renamed Brahmo Samaj in 1830.

questions.question: Indian Railway was introduced in the year __________.
questions.solution:
• First Railway: 1853
  • Fact: The first passenger train ran between Bori Bunder (Bombay) and Thane on April 16, 1853.

questions.question: Who founded a reformist organisation called ‘Brahmo Samaj’ in Calcutta?
questions.solution:
• Brahmo Samaj Founder: Raja Ram Mohan Roy
  • Role: Known as the 'Father of Modern India', he worked tirelessly against Sati and idol worship.

questions.question: In the 11th century, under Maḥmūd of Ghazni, Ghaznī, a small town in ______, became the capital of the vast empire of the Ghaznavids.
questions.solution:
• Ghazni Location: Afghanistan
  • Context: Mahmud of Ghazni transformed this small town into a center of Islamic culture and power in the 11th century.

questions.question: Which military officer led the British forces in the Battle of Chinhat fought in 1857?
questions.solution:
• Battle of Chinhat: Henry Lawrence
  • 1857 Revolt: This battle was fought near Lucknow; the British suffered a major defeat against the Indian rebels.

questions.question: At which place did Raja Ram Mohan Roy form a reform association called Brahmo Sabha in the year 1828?
questions.solution:
• Brahmo Sabha Place: Calcutta
  • Year: 1828. It was the first major socio-religious reform organization in India.

questions.question: Which amongst the following Sultans shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
questions.solution:
• Capital Shift: Muhammad Bin Tughlaq
  • History: He shifted the capital in 1327 to have a more central location to rule South India, but the experiment failed.

questions.question: Which Act opposed by Mahatma Gandhi in 1919 was a direct attack on the civil liberties and democratic rights of the Indian people?
questions.solution:
• Rowlatt Act (1919): Rowlatt Act
  • Fact: Known as the 'Black Act', it allowed the government to imprison people without trial for up to two years.

questions.question: The founder of the Pallava dynasty was:
questions.solution:
• Pallava Founder: Simhavishnu
  • Reign: He started the era of the 'Great Pallavas' by conquering the Chola territory.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• Bahmani Sultanate Founder: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah
  • Original Name: Hasan Gangu. He founded the first independent Islamic kingdom in South India in 1347.

questions.question: Who founded the Bombay Presidency Association in 1885 along with Pherozeshah Mehta and KT Telang?
questions.solution:
• Bombay Presidency Association: Badruddin Tyabji
  • Trio: Known as the 'Three Bright Stars' of Bombay’s public life (Mehta, Telang, and Tyabji).

questions.question: What was the name of the campaign led by the Ali brothers and Maulana Abul Kalam Azad to save the Ottoman Caliphate as a symbol of unity among the Muslim community?
questions.solution:
• Khilafat Movement: Khilafat Movement
  • Goal: To protest against the dismemberment of the Ottoman Empire after WWI. It was supported by Gandhi during Non-Cooperation.

questions.question: Bilhan was a court poet in which of the following kingdoms?
questions.solution:
• Bilhan's Patron: Vikramaditya VI
  • Literature: Bilhan wrote 'Vikramankadevacharita' in honor of his patron, the Western Chalukya King.

questions.question: Who amongst the following Mughal emperors got classical Hindu mythological texts Ramayana and Mahabharata translated into Persian?
questions.solution:
• Akbar's Translations: Akbar
  • Detail: He established a 'Maktab Khana' (Translation Bureau) to translate Sanskrit epics into Persian (e.g., Razmnama for Mahabharata).

questions.question: Warren Hastings became the Governor-General of Bengal from Governor of Bengal after the passing of which of the following Acts?
questions.solution:
• Regulating Act 1773: Regulating Act, 1773
  • Change: It unified the three presidencies and made the Governor of Bengal the Governor-General of all British territories in India.

questions.question: Which revolutionary organisation was established at Feroz Shah Kotla in New Delhi in 1928?
questions.solution:
• HSRA (1928): Hindustan Socialist Republican Association
  • Leaders: Established by Bhagat Singh, Chandrashekhar Azad, and Sukhdev at Feroz Shah Kotla.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements about Akbar are true?

1 He introduced the Mansabdari system.

2 He defeated and merged the state of Bijapur in his empire.

3 He made Fatehpur Sikri his capital.
questions.solution:
• Akbar Facts: Only 1 and 3
  • Correction: Aurangzeb, not Akbar, finally merged Bijapur (1886) into the Mughal Empire.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Sanchi Stupa UNESCO world heritage site located?
questions.solution:
• Sanchi Stupa Location: Madhya Pradesh
  • Architecture: Originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE.

questions.question: The founder of the Pala empire was:
questions.solution:
• Pala Founder: Gopala
  • Fact: He was elected by the people to end the state of anarchy (Matsyanyaya) in Bengal.

questions.question: Which was the first socio-religious organisation established in Bombay in 1840 to work for the annihilation of caste?
questions.solution:
• Paramhans Mandali: Paramhans Mandali
  • 1840: A secret socio-religious group in Bombay that advocated for the abolition of caste and the breaking of food taboos.

questions.question: Which important event that started in 1930 played a significant role in motivating and mobilizing Indians to join the non-violent movement for independence?
questions.solution:
• Salt Satyagraha: Salt Satyagraha
  • 1930: Began with the Dandi March; it was the start of the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.question: Annamacharya composed Sankirtans in praise of which God?
questions.solution:
• Annamacharya: Lord Venkateshwara
  • Music: He is the earliest known Indian musician to compose songs called 'Sankirtanas' in Telugu.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the National Anthem adopted in its Hindi version by the Constituent Assembly?
questions.solution:
• National Anthem Adoption: 1950
  • Date: Adopted on January 24, 1950. It was originally composed in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore.
